pages.name: Home
pages.purpose: App home screen. Two big choices: send files or receive files. Shown on launch.
pages.notes: Portrait. App title, tagline and any helper text are live text drawn by code, so keep those areas free of lettering. Buttons are separate images (normal + pressed) placed over the background; the button labels are drawn by code too unless you tell me otherwise.

pages.name: Sending
pages.purpose: Shown while the phone is sharing files. Shows the QR code and link for the other phone, plus a live list of what has been sent.
pages.notes: The QR code is generated by the app and must sit on a plain WHITE square at least 640 px wide (QR needs the contrast), so leave that area empty and white. The link text, file count and the activity log are live text. Do not paint any of those.

pages.name: Receiving
pages.purpose: Shown while the phone is waiting to receive files. Shows the QR code and link for the sender, plus a live list of files that arrived.
pages.notes: Same layout idea as Sending but with its own look so people can tell the two apart at a glance. QR needs a plain white square of at least 640 px. All text (link, status, file names, sizes) is live.

pages.name: Allow device
pages.purpose: Version 0.2 prompt: when a new phone or browser tries to connect, the host must tap Allow or Deny before anything transfers.
pages.notes: Shown as a dialog panel floating over the Sending/Receiving screen, so the art is the panel plus buttons, not a full screen. The device name, its address and the message text are live text. Keep the panel stretchable.

pages.name: Web download page
pages.purpose: Web page the OTHER phone's browser shows when this phone is SENDING: a list of files to tap and download.
pages.notes: This is an HTML/CSS page, not an Android screen. Design it as a mobile-width page. I will turn your art into CSS backgrounds and embed it in the app. Keep image files small (the app serves them over a hotspot): background under 150 KB if you can, use WebP/PNG. File names and sizes are live rows, so show an empty row design.

pages.name: Web upload page
pages.purpose: Web page the OTHER phone's browser shows when this phone is RECEIVING: choose files, tap Upload, see progress per file.
pages.notes: HTML/CSS page. Design for mobile width. Needs: a file-choose button, an Upload button, and progress rows for each file (progress bar is drawn by the page). Keep images small, same as the download page.
